correctness.rationale: For 1<p<∞ and every integer r≥0, the matrix identity (H_i-H_j)^r/i follows by iterated diagonal commutation; the sorted-tuple inequality K_r≤r! C^(r+1) plus sharp Hardy norm gives the global upper bound. Truncated power-law inputs on each tail converge to the gamma integral r!/(1-1/p)^(r+1), giving equality on each tail; compact-adjoint tail convergence establishes identical essential norm. The exact-rational coefficient checker passed dimensions 1–22, orders 0–5 and numerical Riemann tests, which are corroborative only.

originality.rationale: The full accessible works on compact power diagonals and bounded periodic diagonals have different kernels and only Hilbert–Schmidt/ideal claims; the exact integer-harmonic all-order, all-p norm plus essential equality is not an implication of those statements. Fu–Lu–Yuan (2012) gives Hardy commutator criteria and logarithmic tests in different spaces; Nie–Yan (2018) supplies the used base Hardy norm. The inaccessible parts of earlier 2002/2003 literature remain risk, so PASS is qualified and not a claim of universal uniqueness.
residual_risks: Unindexed or differently phrased priority claims in older Hardy–Cesàro and commutator literature cannot be excluded.
Long–Wang (2002), Zhao (2012), and Komori (2003) full texts were not all accessible; no whole-document noncoverage is asserted for them.
Some equations in the publisher HTML extraction for Fu–Lu–Yuan (2012) are image/formula placeholders; the accessible paragraphs and scope comparisons are informative but not exhaustive.

Earlier sources from 2002–2003 have no verified exact first-public day; the metadata date 2012-03-05 identifies the earliest precisely dated inspected lead source, not the invention of an older public release date.

value.rationale: The harmonic-number diagonal is a canonical discretization of logarithmic dilation and is itself unbounded. A complete formula for every commutator order and every 1<p<∞, with equality of full and essential norm and a sharp operator Taylor radius, provides exact stability and noncompactness beyond generic boundedness. The factorial dependence and tail rigidity are motivated structural invariants rather than arbitrary finite examples.
